verdicts.trueWording: “‘V.R.T’ is told anachronically, with the reader left to piece everything together from a fragmentary, disjointed narrative”
verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched from ultan.org.uk (HTTP 200, browser UA). Quote is contiguous and word-for-word. Both limbs supported: 'told anachronically' and the piecing-together clause sit in the same sentence. Byline on the page: 'reviewed by Robert Borski', dated 28 August 2001 — attribution confirmed.

verdicts.trueWording: “the only name he’s identified by in the book: Number Five (though both his first and last name are eminently decodeable)”
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim. The decodeable-names limb is the page's own parenthesis. Page says 'in the book' where the claim says 'the first novella's narrator'; the surrounding sentence is about Maitre and the narrator of the title novella, so the narrowing is accurate rather than a stretch.

verdicts.trueWording: “Rich eccentricities of diction abound, retarding comprehension.”
verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched from ultan.org.uk (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim. Second limb supported: the paragraph then itemises Tick, Oreb, the lower classes' 'thieves' cant', the lower-ranking soldiers, Remora, Incus, the Trivigaunti elite, Quetzal, Crane, Lemur. Locator nit only: the section is headed 'Dialogue.', not 'Voices' — the claim sentence itself does not assert the heading.

verdicts.trueWording: “As Wolfe’s narrator years afterwards reconstructs Silk’s story from his own memories and from much oral testimony”
verdicts.note: Same raw page, opening of the 'Plot.' section. Quote verbatim; the 'years afterwards' limb is on the page too, immediately before the quoted span.

verdicts.trueWording: “Sometimes events are related in great, possibly very significant detail; elsewhere, complex developments are told at second hand”
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same 'Plot.' sentence. Quote verbatim; the second-hand limb is the following clause of the same sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: “or conveyed speedily and with gaping lacunae”
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same sentence. Quote verbatim as a contiguous span.

verdicts.trueWording: “in certain instances, only guesswork can reconstruct what has occurred”
verdicts.note: Same raw page, closing clause of the same 'Plot.' sentence. Quote verbatim; the subject throughout is the Long Sun narrative.

verdicts.trueWording: “Detailed textual analysis, of the kind all Wolfe’s works demand, suggests that the Outsider has two oracular mouthpieces”
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim. It does sit in the Oreb/Quetzal discussion, as the locator says, and the claim's paraphrase (all Wolfe's works demand detailed textual analysis) is the page's own assertion.

verdicts.trueWording: “Wolfe tells us that the torturers are the executors of a sentence decided elsewhere by the judicial process.”
verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched from ultan.org.uk (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim, and the claim's added words 'by the judicial process' are the page's own continuation. Byline 'by Jeremy Crampton', dated 10 April 2001, signed 'Jeremy Crampton, October-December 2000' — attribution confirmed. Subject is Wolfe's Book of the New Sun throughout.

verdicts.trueWording: “The silence of the torturer also emphasises that the confession is not there for the benefit of the torturers, but to produce penitence in the accused, or to produce truth for the authorities”
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim. The claim compresses 'penitence in the accused, or ... truth for the authorities (be it judge or priest)' to 'penitence or truth for the authorities'; that reads the page correctly rather than adding to it.

verdicts.trueWording: “that his system should approximate so closely that of Europe up to the early modern period”
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim; the full sentence is 'It is all the more interesting therefore that his system should approximate so closely that of Europe up to the early modern period.' It sits at ~86% through the article, in the closing discussion — consistent with the 'conclusion' locator.

verdicts.trueWording: “1) Trust the text implicitly. The answers are in there.”
